summary: Boris, a member of technical staff at Anthropic and creator of Claude Code, opens by stating a core principle: the more general model always wins, and model capabilities increase exponentially. He notes there are many areas affected by this trend. He references Anthropic's recent announcement that Claude can now be used on GitHub, highlighting the integration between AI coding tools and developer workflows. Boris then shares two practical use cases he employs regularly. First, for weekly Monday standup meetings, he asks Claude Code to review his git commits and summarize what he shipped that week, eliminating the need to manually track his work. Second, he discusses Test-Driven Development (TDD), acknowledging that while he tries to use TDD, it is difficult to practice in reality. However, with AI coding tools like Claude Code, TDD works well. Boris suggests the key reason is that the model performs the TDD process rather than the human developer, removing the friction that typically makes TDD challenging to adopt. The talk concludes with applause, aligning with the video's themes of GitHub integration, TDD workflows, the Bitter Lesson principle, and developer productivity through AI-assisted coding.
